cards.method: Series layout conversion + basic transformations (convert/diff/pc/index/scale/lag/aggregate/span/combine/summary)
cards.when: after the fetch; converting between the long, wide and indexed layouts + the standard analyst transformations (diff/%/index/z/lag/aggregate/span)
cards.when_not: charts (the frontend); INCREASING the frequency -> #79; filling gaps -> #80 (ts_fill_regular only inserts the empty rows)

alternatives.criterion: you need explicit macro conventions + post-checks (annualize/deflate/contributions additivity)
consistency-preserving aggregation is not needed -> plain aggregate suffices

output_key_fields: series: the transformed object (a single series -> {values, start, frequency}; a matrix -> nested rows; a frame -> records)
class/n/freq: compact metadata + applied arguments
transform: pc=q/q%, pcy=YoY%, pca=annualized pc, diff=plain difference
interpretation_traps: ts_rebase/ts_index: index=1 (NOT 100); base=A DATE (NOT a number); base=100 errors -> for base=100 see macro_rebase #82
ts_aggregate: ONLY towards a lower frequency (hard gate)
the time column is detected from its dtype (date or datetime) — a long uploaded frame is taken as it comes
sources: Wickham 2014 JSS 59(10) (Tidy Data — the long/wide layout contract)

cards.method: Temporal (dis)aggregation of series (Chow-Lin/Fernandez/Litterman/Denton disaggregation + aggregation)
cards.when: consistency-preserving frequency change; low->high (td, with/without an indicator) or high->low (ta, sum/average/first/last)
cards.when_not: plain aggregation with no consistency constraint -> ts_aggregate (#78); scattered gaps -> #80; forecasting

alternatives.criterion: with an indicator, broad range (recommended)
underlying series I(1)/random-walk-like
WITHOUT an indicator, smooth interpolation

output_key_fields: disaggregated: high-frequency series (->{values,start,frequency}) — the main result
low_span/high_span: requested vs realized spans (data-integrity)
coefficients/se/rho/method/conversion/fr + r_squared/aic/bic/logl/rss (GLS regression stats)
residuals/fitted_low/actual: LOW-frequency (input level, not output)
interpretation_traps: SPAN GATE: the indicator MUST cover the low-freq series; otherwise silent truncation/extrapolation -> escalated to stop
the Denton methods leave the regression statistics empty — NOT a 'bad fit'; there is no regression to report
conversion must match: flow->sum, index/rate->average, stock->last/first (wrong = consistent but WRONG)
sources: Sax & Steiner, Temporal Disaggregation of Time Series, 5(2):80-88, 2013 (doi:10.32614/RJ-2013-028)
Chow & Lin 1971 (Rev. Econ. Stat. 372-375)
Santos Silva & Cardoso 2001 (Economic Modelling 18:269, dynamic Chow-Lin)

cards.method: Replacement of missing values in time series (Kalman / interpolation / seasonally-decomposed + a missingness report)
cards.when: scattered internal gaps; mapping the pattern (impute_missing_stats) + filling for methods that do not tolerate gaps (VAR/filters/ACF)
cards.when_not: a frequency difference rather than a gap -> #79; a missing tail, which is forecasting -> category 02; gaps that must stay unfilled -> ts_fill_regular (#78)

alternatives.criterion: series with trend/seasonality, medium gaps
fast, model-free, small gaps
strong seasonality to preserve (requires ts freq>1, >=2 periods)

output_key_fields: imputed: ts/numeric (->{values,start,frequency}) + parameters
n_imputed: the positions that were filled; n_remaining_na: those left unfilled (runs longer than maxgap)
na_report: statsNA as data (length/number/percentage_NAs numeric/gaps/longest/most_weighty)
interpretation_traps: n_remaining_na>0 is NOT an error — it is the deliberate maxgap cut-off (long runs stay unfilled)
algorithm='random' is stochastic -> an enforced seed (default 42L) for reproducibility
bins affects ONLY the print table; gap_distribution is UNBINNED (per exact gap length)
imputed values carry no uncertainty — take care if they enter inference as observations
sources: Moritz & Bartz-Beielstein 2017, 9(1):207-218 (time series missing value imputation)
Harvey 1990 (Forecasting, Structural TS Models and the Kalman Filter)
Hyndman & Khandakar 2008 JSS 27(3) (automatic time series forecasting)

cards.method: Descriptive statistics as data (ACF/PACF/CCF/rolling/correlation matrix + per-pair correlation inference)
cards.when: pre-model exploration/diagnostics; ARMA order id (ACF/PACF), lead/lag (CCF), rolling stats, correlation matrix — all numeric data; desc_cor_test when you need INFERENCE (p-values/CI) per pair with multiplicity control
cards.when_not: formal stationarity (ACF is indicative -> ADF/KPSS cat.01); causality (CCF != Granger); partial/conditional correlation (conditioning on third variables -> regression cat.06/07); autocorrelated series without prewhitening (the i.i.d. null of cor_test is violated -> inflated Type I)

alternatives.alt: ACF cut-off -> MA(q), PACF cut-off -> AR(p)
alternatives.criterion: Box-Jenkins order identification — use them together
rank-based, robust to non-linearity/outliers vs pearson (linear)
smoothing (non-causal) vs align=right (causal, default)

desc_correlations = POINT estimates (p×p matrix, no hypothesis, no p-value) -> exploration/heatmap. desc_cor_test = per-pair INFERENCE (statistic, df, p-value, conf_int) + MANDATORY multiplicity correction. The point estimates are IDENTICAL (test-covered) — the difference is ONLY the inference

BH controls the FDR (more powerful, for screening many pairs); holm/hochberg/hommel/bonferroni control the FWER (when EVERY false positive is costly). Bonferroni is dominated by holm — use holm. The alias 'fdr' is NOT exposed (identical to BH)

pairwise = the maximum n per pair but a DIFFERENT sample per pair (the p-values are not strictly comparable); complete = a listwise drop giving a COMMON sample across all pairs (comparable, smaller n); 'raise' = a hard stop on any missing value

output_key_fields: acf/pacf/ccf: numeric + lag + n_used; ci_upper/ci_lower = ±1.96/sqrt(n) white-noise band
desc_rolling: the rolled series (index-aligned, blank at the edges) + the index
desc_correlations: correlation (matrix->nested+axis labels), n=rows supplied, n_pairwise=per-pair complete

desc_cor_test: pairs = long-format records PER PAIR (var1, var2, n, estimate, statistic, statistic_name, parameter, p_value, p_adjusted, conf_low, conf_high, ties, exact_used); ALWAYS read p_adjusted, NOT p_value
desc_cor_test: pair_order = an EXPLICIT deterministic order (upper triangle by COLUMN INDEX (1,2),(1,3),..,(p-1,p) — NOT alphabetical), so that stored workflows reproduce (§5)
desc_cor_test: n_rows_input / n_rows_used / n_missing_cells (n_missing_cells is measured BEFORE the listwise drop); any_ties / any_exact_fallback / warnings = degradation flags
interpretation_traps: non-stationary series: the ACF decays slowly and linearly (an artefact, not structure) — test stationarity first

CCF: with ccf(x, y) (as the wrapper calls it) lag k estimates cor(x[t+k], y[t]) -> NEGATIVE lags = x leads y (x leads, peak at lag<0), POSITIVE lags = x lags behind (y leads); confirm the lag sign in the raw object before concluding lead/lag
desc_correlations: with pairwise completion and gaps the scalar n OVERSTATES — read n_pairwise (a strong correlation on a small n_pairwise is fragile)

desc_cor_test: Kendall and Spearman define NEITHER a confidence interval NOR degrees of freedom — the wrapper returns an explicit blank in conf_low/conf_high/parameter, NEVER a silently omitted field. The interval is defined only for Pearson, and only on at least 4 complete pairs (live-verified)

desc_cor_test: with ties cor_test silently DOWNGRADES the exact p-value to an asymptotic approximation and ONLY warns ('cannot compute exact p-value with ties'). The wrapper exposes this as DATA: ties / exact_used / any_exact_fallback / warnings (each warning carries its pair). Check exact_used before trusting small p-values

desc_cor_test: for spearman with n>1290 AS 89 is abandoned silently (WITHOUT a warning) in favour of the t-approximation. the cor_test routine states 'n < 1290' while the stats code checks 'n <= 1290' — the wrapper encodes the CODE (live-verified), which is why exact_used is reliable

desc_cor_test: on a constant (zero-variance) column the correlation test does NOT error — it ONLY warns ('the standard deviation is zero') and returns a blank estimate and p-value (live-verified for all 3 methods). The wrapper makes this a HARD GATE, per column AND per pair: a column can have variance overall yet be constant on the rows a given pair shares

desc_cor_test: for pearson cor_test SILENTLY ignores exact/continuity (live-verified: identical p-value, no warning) -> the wrapper makes them a hard gate so the user does not think they had an effect

desc_cor_test: the i.i.d. null of cor_test is violated for autocorrelated macro series -> inflated Type I error. For lead/lag in time series use desc_ccf (with prewhitening) or Granger (cat.06), NOT desc_cor_test on raw levels

desc_cor_test: the single n>=4 gate is DELIBERATELY stricter than the per-method minimum (pearson n>=3, kendall/spearman n>=2 — live-verified) so that the output schema does not change silently with the method; at n=2/3 kendall/spearman return a degenerate |r|=1 with p=1
sources: Box, Jenkins & Reinsel, Time Series Analysis: Forecasting and Control (ACF/PACF order id)
Enders 2015 Applied Econometric Time Series 4th ed. §2 (correlogram)
the cor_test routine (the engine) — the exact rules: Kendall for n<50, the Spearman AS 89 algorithm, an interval only for Pearson on >=4 complete pairs, and the tie definition with its n<=1290 cutoff
the p_adjust routine (the engine) — BH/BY/holm/hochberg/hommel/bonferroni; 'BH' (alias 'fdr')
Benjamini & Hochberg (1995), JRSS-B 57(1):289-300, doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x (FDR — default BH)
Holm (1979), Scand. J. Statist. 6:65-70 (step-down FWER; dominates Bonferroni)
Benjamini & Yekutieli (2001), Ann. Statist. 29(4), doi:10.1214/aos/1013699998 (FDR under dependence — BY)
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/replacement_missing_values.impute_kalman (fill the gaps first — the input gate rejects gaps and infinities)

cards.method: Macro arithmetic (growth/annualize/deflate/rebase/per-capita/contributions)
cards.when: deterministic macro identities with explicit conventions; rate/annualize, nominal->real, index rebase, per-capita, contributions + additivity check
cards.when_not: layout-agnostic transformations without macro semantics -> #78; chain-linked data where the contributions are not additive (the residual is exposed)

alternatives.criterion: macro_growth when you need an explicit annualization convention + div-by-zero flag
additively decomposable, large changes/aggregation vs simple growth (direct %)
vs ts_rebase #78 (base=1, date-anchored)

output_key_fields: macro_growth: the growth series (structurally blank at the first observation), annualized, annualize_convention, n_nonfinite_growth (the divide-by-zero flag)
macro_deflate: real=nominal/deflator*base; macro_rebase: index+anchor; macro_per_capita: x/population*scale
macro_contributions: contributions (matrix), contribution_total, additivity_checked/max_abs_residual/checks_passed
interpretation_traps: compound annualization for simple growth: q/q 1% -> (1.01)^4-1 = 4.06% (NOT 4%); log: g*(freq/periods), linear
n_nonfinite_growth/annualized>0 = a silent NaN (zero/negative base) which to_mcp turns into null; check it explicitly
macro_contributions takes GROWTH RATES per component (column)/period (row), NOT levels; additivity fail -> hard stop
sources: the standard library (arithmetic identities, no external dependency)
annualization compound convention (live-verified in the wrapper)
log-growth additivity (Tornqvist/log-diff decomposition, standard)
precondition_tools: c00_data_utilities/replacement_missing_values.impute_kalman (fill the gaps first — the finite gate rejects gaps, NaN and infinities)

cards.method: Reading delimited / fixed-width flat files (CSV/TSV/delim/FWF) + parse-problem diagnostics
cards.when: the first step of the DAG; ingest a user-uploaded flat file -> a long/records data_frame (register data -> Parquet); parse problems as data
cards.when_not: Excel -> #97; Parquet/Feather -> #98; JSON -> #99; Stata/SPSS/SAS -> #100; charts (the frontend); a custom locale or fixed-width spec -> the L1 wrapper

alternatives.criterion: a large/columnar CSV or Arrow type inference; no fine-grained parse diagnostics
columnar fixed width with no delimiter

output_key_fields: data: plain data_frame -> records (registered producer -> Parquet)
col_names/column_types/n_rows/n_cols: the detected structure
problems/n_problems/has_problems: parse diagnostics (the file column is dropped)
interpretation_traps: the read is eager internally so that parse problems materialise IMMEDIATELY; a lazy default would leave them empty
a whitespace-only file silently yields a 0x0 frame -> blocked (no column)
col_types is a compact string (e.g. 'Dd'), NOT a per-column vector; locale/col_positions are not exposed on the node
sources: RFC 4180 (the common format and MIME type for comma-separated values)
validation_notes: path: a non-empty string, NOT a directory, existing, size>0 bytes
POST-gate ncol>0 (a whitespace-only file yields a silent 0x0 frame)
col_types unset, a compact string, or a full column spec; the missing-value markers a non-empty list of strings with no blank entry; and read_delimited takes a delimiter of EXACTLY one character

cards.method: Reading/writing Excel workbooks (.xls/.xlsx read + sheet discovery +.xlsx write)
cards.when: ingest an Excel upload -> a rectangular data_frame (register data -> Parquet); sheet/range selection; xl_write is a terminal export
cards.when_not: CSV/TSV -> #96; Parquet/Feather -> #98; Stata/SPSS/SAS -> #100; styling or plotting (the frontend)

alternatives.criterion: the modern workbook format only, with row names, a start row and date detection; NOT the legacy format nor an A1 range
the legacy workbook format, or an A1 range subset

output_key_fields: data: the frame -> records (a registered producer -> Parquet) + nrow/ncol/columns/sheet
xl_sheet_names: sheets (character) + n_sheets
xl_write: file/sheets_written/n_sheets/bytes
interpretation_traps: CRITICAL: writing something that is not a frame (or a list of frames) does NOT error -> a silently empty workbook -> hard gate
reading an empty sheet returns nothing -> normalised to a 0-row frame
xl_read_workbook does NOT read the legacy format, only the modern one; sheet is a 1-indexed position
sources: ECMA-376 (Office Open XML file formats) — the workbook layout and the A1 range grammar
validation_notes: path a non-empty string that must exist; sheet validated against the real list of sheets
the range pre-validated as an A1 cell range; col_types in {skip, guess, logical, numeric, date, text, list}
xl_read_workbook rejects the legacy format; xl_write checks the extension and the overwrite flag

cards.method: Canonical on-disk data-format layer: Parquet/Feather/CSV readers + a Parquet writer + a lazy (hive-)partitioned Dataset
cards.when: Parquet/Feather/CSV, the lingua franca of the object store; the readers register data -> Parquet; the writer df->Parquet; open_dataset is lazy and partitioned
cards.when_not: parse diagnostics or an explicit column spec -> #96; Excel -> #97; JSON -> #99; NEVER an opaque columnar table (as_data_frame=False)

alternatives.criterion: a CSV with parse-problem diagnostics; not a large columnar file/type inference
hive-partitioned multiple files in a directory (lazy); not a single eager file

output_key_fields: data: plain data_frame (registered producer -> Parquet) + schema/n_rows/n_cols/columns/format
writer: path/bytes/schema/compression (NOT a producer)
open_dataset: a lazy dataset stub + JSON-safe schema/partitioning/files/preview
interpretation_traps: CRITICAL: a col_select whose variable is empty selects ZERO columns silently -> read everything and subset afterwards
the codec (zstd/gzip) is compile-time optional -> gated with codec_is_available
the readers ALWAYS materialise a plain data_frame (never an opaque Arrow Table)
sources: the Apache Parquet and Apache Arrow columnar format specifications
validation_notes: read_*: file = an existing FILE (not a directory); a cryptic IOError otherwise
write_parquet: x a data_frame with >=1 column; the parent dir of sink exists; codec_is_available; POST-gate the file was created
open_dataset: sources = an existing DIRECTORY; n_preview >= 0 integer

cards.method: JSON interchange: parse / serialise / validate / NDJSON stream in-out
cards.when: the JSON/NDJSON data layer; json_parse/json_stream_parse are producers (register); json_write/stream_write are serializers; json_validate is a diagnostic
cards.when_not: CSV -> #96; Excel -> #97; Parquet -> #98; for tabular data prefer #96/#98; file IO belongs to the reader and writer nodes

alternatives.criterion: NDJSON newline-delimited records -> a data_frame; not a single JSON document
purely tabular data (Parquet/CSV) instead of nested/semi-structured JSON

output_key_fields: json_parse: parsed (vector/list/data_frame, registered; df->Parquet otherwise RDS) + type/n
json_stream_parse: data (data_frame -> Parquet) + n/ncol
json_write/json_stream_write: json/ndjson/text strings; json_validate valid/error/offset
interpretation_traps: CRITICAL: the serialiser defaults to 4 significant digits and rounds SILENTLY (pi -> 3.1416) -> the wrapper disables the rounding
auto_unbox=True (the default): length-1 arrays become JSON scalars
fromJSON auto-fetching a URL/path is blocked by the validate-first rule (no SSRF)
sources: Ooms 2014 (arXiv:1403.2805) — a mapping between JSON data and statistical data types
validation_notes: json_parse: txt a single non-empty string; validate FIRST, which blocks both malformed input AND any attempt to fetch a URL or a file
json_write: digits unset means full precision; force=False, so a value with no JSON mapping is a hard error
json_stream_parse: text with no blank entry; EVERY line is validated before the stream; json_stream_write requires at least one row

cards.method: Import/export Stata/SPSS/SAS (.dta/.sav/.sas7bdat) with labelled metadata + labelled-to-categorical materialisation
cards.when: ingest an uploaded .dta/.sav/.sas7bdat -> a long-format frame (register data -> Parquet) + the variable and value labels; sfile_write_stata exports; sfile_labels_to_categorical turns a labelled column into a categorical
cards.when_not: CSV -> #96; Excel -> #97; Parquet -> #98; JSON -> #99; the secondary formats (.por/.xpt, SPSS write); URL or stream inputs (a local path only)

alternatives.criterion: choose by file format (.dta/.sav/.sas7bdat)
categorical analysis/plots on haven_labelled columns before the downstream step

output_key_fields: data: the frame (a registered producer -> Parquet; labelled columns as numeric codes)
var_labels/value_labels/labelled_cols/col_types/dataset_label: JSON-safe metadata
writer: path/written/version/n_rows/n_cols/bytes; as_factor: data/input_type/levels/n
interpretation_traps: the column attribute 'label' PARTIAL-matches 'labels' (the value labels) when the variable label is absent -> an exact lookup everywhere
write_dta version=14.5 is accepted SILENTLY; version=c(14,15) gives a cryptic length error -> a whole-number length-1 gate
as_factor on a plain numeric -> forcats silently produces a factor (silently wrong) -> a labelled-only gate
sources: the Stata .dta, SPSS .sav and SAS .sas7bdat file-format specifications
validation_notes: read path: a string of length 1, NOT a directory, existing; write path: the parent dir exists + a POST-gate that it was written
the data to write must be a frame with at least one column; version a single integer in 8-15; and the label either unset or at most 80 bytes
sfile_labels_to_categorical: a non-df input MUST be labelled (otherwise forcats silently turns every vector into a factor)

cards.method: CLOSED-vocabulary tabular manipulation (filter/select/mutate/arrange/summarise/group_by/join/distinct/rename/relocate/slice)
cards.when: the relational and wrangling layer; filtering, selecting and transforming columns + a per-group aggregation + joins by column name; a CLOSED enum, never a free expression
cards.when_not: free-form expressions (structurally excluded); long/wide reshaping and gap handling -> #102; grouped or panel series transformations -> #103; random sampling (excluded)

alternatives.criterion: grouped/panel numeric series transformation (lags/diffs/growth/within/scale) — faster, g/t panel-aware
reshaping/completion instead of relational operations

output_key_fields: data: the transformed data_frame (records) + n_rows/n_cols/columns
tab_group_by: group_keys/group_sizes/n_groups (a terminal info node — it does NOT chain a grouped_df)
tab_aggregate: <stat>_<column>, or n; tab_join: the join type and the keys
interpretation_traps: tab_group_by is an INFO node; the grouped_df attribute is lost at the Parquet boundary -> use tab_aggregate(by=) for per-group aggregation
tab_assign div/log/sqrt -> NaN/Inf cells; the warning is muffled into a message; the numerical validity is your responsibility
tab_filter: a silently-wrong gate — a numeric column vs a non-numeric value (1=='a' -> 0 rows) is blocked
sources: Codd 1970 CACM 13(6) (a relational model of data for large shared data banks) — the select/filter/join/aggregate vocabulary

cards.method: Tidy-data reshaping & missing-value handling (pivot_longer/pivot_wider/separate_wider/unite/drop_na/replace_na/fill/complete/nest/unnest)
cards.when: table shaping: long/wide, splitting and joining columns, completing combinations, dropping/replacing/forward-filling gaps; a CLOSED vocabulary (columns BY NAME, never a free expression)
cards.when_not: relational operations -> #101; deep rectangling or grid builders (omitted); statistical imputation -> #80; layout or frequency conversion -> #78

alternatives.criterion: relational operations (filter/mutate/join/summarise) instead of reshaping
fast summary/aggregation instead of completion

output_key_fields: data: the reshaped frame (records; nested columns recursively) + dtype/nrow/ncol/column labels
n_dropped (drop_na) / n_added (complete)
pivot_wider: values_fn applied; separate_wider: mode/col
interpretation_traps: shape_pivot with an empty id_cols infers it from the remaining columns; the wrapper omits the argument entirely rather than passing an empty one, which would reduce the result to a single row of nested cells
values_fn: with a unique key -> do not supply an aggregator; with a non-unique key -> you MUST (SILENT list-col gate)
separate_wider_regex: it has NO too_many; too_few='debug' -> a warning (muffled) + debug columns
sources: Wickham 2014 JSS 59(10) (Tidy Data)

cards.method: Fast (grouped/panel) data transformation (growth/diff/lag/cumsum/scale/within/aggregate/summary/generic transform)
cards.when: a high-performance transform layer for series and PANELS; lags/diffs/growth/cumsum/scale/within + multi-column aggregation + a quick summary + a generic transform-and-replace; panel support through the group and time keys, compiled speed, gap-skipping
cards.when_not: relational operations -> #101; long/wide -> #102; macro-semantic transforms (index base=100, deflate, contributions) -> #78 / #82; rolling windows -> #105

alternatives.criterion: you need macro semantics (annualize/deflate/base=100 index/contributions) rather than a mechanical fast transform
small non-panel aggregations; collap wins on speed/multi-column work

output_key_fields: series: the transformed object (series, matrix or frame); stubs=False -> clean column names
fast_aggregate: the aggregated frame; fast_summary: the summary as a plain frame
class/n + the applied arguments
interpretation_traps: fscale/fwithin on a constant series -> a NaN z-score (honest, not silent)
fast_aggregate weights: only the weighted fast-stat functions (mean/sum/median/sd/prod) use them; first/last/min/max/nobs ignore them (the warning is muffled)
fast_summary on a data_frame: supply g (routed to by); qsu_default ignores g SILENTLY
sources: Krantz 2025 JSS 116(1) (advanced and fast statistical data transformation)

cards.method: Deterministic invertible preprocessing transforms (diff/standardize/normalize/box_cox/auto_lambda + lag/difference augmentation + pad_by_time)
cards.when: the feature-engineering layer; EXACTLY invertible preprocessing for a forecasting/ML node (differencing/standardize/normalize/Box-Cox + lag/diff augmentation + regular-timestamp padding)
cards.when_not: charts (the frontend); grouped or panel fast transforms -> #103; macro growth or index -> #82; rolling smoothing -> #105; imputation -> #80

alternatives.criterion: panel-aware (g/t) fast differencing/scaling without inversion parameters
a macro convention (annualize/deflate) rather than reversible ML preprocessing

output_key_fields: result: the transformed vector + the INVERSION PARAMETERS (initial_values/mean/sd/min/max/lambda)
the augmenters: the resulting frame + new_columns + dimensions
prep_box_cox: lambda ('auto' -> selected & reported)
interpretation_traps: Box-Cox/auto_lambda require x>0; log=True requires x>0 (otherwise SILENT NaN); lambda_lower<upper (an inverted interval is accepted silently -> gate)
prep_diff_inverse needs EXACTLY the initial_values & lag/difference of prep_diff for a full inversion
a constant series -> standardize/normalize give NaN (gated); auto_lambda is deterministic (an identical lambda, no seed)
sources: Box & Cox 1964 JRSS-B 26(2) (an analysis of transformations)

cards.method: Deterministic rolling-window aggregations (positional / index / calendar-period / arbitrary-pair windows)
cards.when: the rolling-aggregate layer; rolling mean/sum/sd/min/max/median in 4 regimes (positional/index-relative/calendar-period/arbitrary pairs); type-stable throughout
cards.when_not: charts (the frontend); diff/growth/lags -> #103/#104; a free custom reducer (structurally excluded); weighted or exponential rolling -> #107/#109

alternatives.criterion: point transforms (diff/growth/scale) rather than window reduction
specialised weighted/EMA rolling

output_key_fields: values: double vector = chart-data (length=length(x) for slide*, =length(starts) for hop)
n/n_na/reducer/na_rm + the applied arguments
empty windows -> NaN/Inf, reported in n_na (they are not hidden)
interpretation_traps: the reducer is NEVER exposed as a callable — it is a closed enum {mean, sum, sd, min, max, median}, which is a security boundary
win_hop_index returns one value per start (NOT one per observation); in win_slide_period the before/after counts are BLOCKS, not observations
before/after: an integer, or infinity; a negative value looks forward; and a non-empty window requires before+after>=0
sources: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd ed., ch.3 (moving averages and rolling windows)

cards.method: Indexed (time-stamped) time-series toolbox (periodicity->OHLC, calendar-period aggregation, index merge/join, intraday alignment)
cards.when: the time or calendar index ITSELF is the subject: OHLC periodicity conversion, calendar aggregation (endpoints, per-period apply, monthly apply), index join, intraday alignment
cards.when_not: plain rolling transforms -> #107/#109/#108; charts (the frontend); INCREASING the frequency -> #79; layout plumbing with no index -> #78

alternatives.criterion: class-agnostic aggregation without OHLC/calendar-endpoint control
a rolling-window statistic rather than a calendar bucket

output_key_fields: series: the indexed result, serialised as {index, values}; the typed object itself travels in the node's binary bucket
class/n/ncol/periodicity + the applied arguments
idx_to_period: ncol=4 OHLC or ncol=1 close; the index is the end of the period
interpretation_traps: idx_to_period on an arbitrary multi-column input SILENTLY builds a misleading OHLC -> a hard gate requiring either a univariate series or a genuine 4-column OHLC
idx_align_time on a date or year-month index is a SILENT no-op -> a hard gate requiring a timestamp index
the OHLC column prefix is the caller's series name (fallback 'V.' for non-symbols); align: n_seconds is separate from the count n
sources: ISO 8601 (date and time representations) — the index contract this card enforces

cards.method: Rolling / windowed series transforms (rate-of-change, momentum, moving-average smoothers, single-series rolling stats, rolling cor/cov)
cards.when: deterministic rolling & rate-of-change transforms on a univariate series: ROC(log/discrete), momentum, MA smoothers, rolling moments, rolling cor/cov
cards.when_not: OHLC price technicals (out of scope); calendar or intraday work -> #106; matrix, panel or rolling regression -> #109; fast lead/lag and rolling apply -> #108; charts (the frontend)

alternatives.criterion: online/weighted rolling, panel/matrix, or rolling regression
C speed on a long series + robust reducers (IQR/mad/prod)
calendar buckets rather than a fixed rolling window

n_obs, n_na: an explicit count of blanks (never a silent drop) + the arguments applied
type: continuous=log return, discrete=simple % return (ROC)
interpretation_traps: rate-of-change and momentum with n greater than the series length return an all-blank result of the wrong length SILENTLY -> n is gated to [1, length]

sources: Kaufman 2013, Trading Systems and Methods, 5th ed. (rate of change, momentum, moving-average smoothers)

weighted/online rolling, a panel matrix, or roll_lm

n_obs, class + the applied arguments
leading and trailing blanks according to the alignment; the padding comes from fill

a multi-offset fl_shift (n=c(1,2)) -> result is a list, not a flat vector

cards.when_not: single-series rate-of-change, momentum or moving averages -> #107; fast lead/lag and rolling-apply reducers -> #108; calendar, OHLC or intraday work -> #106; charts (the frontend)

alternatives.alt: #108 fast rolling mean and rolling apply
alternatives.criterion: ONE series, C speed & robust reducers, without weighted/online/panel support
classic rolling moments/cor on a short univariate series

rll_lm: coefficients/r_squared/std_error (matrices, 1 row per observation) + n/width/min_obs/online — NOT a chainable producer
class/shape (n or dim) + width/min_obs/online (+center/scale/p)
interpretation_traps: width>nobs or min_obs>width => SILENTLY all-blank; a fractional or text width is silently truncated or coerced -> hard gates

cards.when_not: weighted or multivariate rolling (correlation, covariance, regression, scaling) -> #109; an irregular index or a custom function -> #105/#108; imputation -> #80; charts -> the frontend

rolling by index/period or with an arbitrary function

output_key_fields: series: the rolling vector (a matrix input -> nested rows)
n: output length (endrule='trim' -> shorter); k/endrule/align + the applied arguments
probs/type/constant/center_supplied: per-method metadata
interpretation_traps: k: a finite integer in [1, nobs] (hard gate); k<=0 => x unchanged, fractional => truncated, k>n => over-run
align='center' requires an ODD k (an even k => a silently asymmetric window); 'right'=trailing (no look-ahead)
endrule='trim' SHORTENS the series; the default endrule fills the edges with the statistic itself
sources: Tukey — running median / MAD robust smoothing

cards.method: Date parsing/rounding/components + safe month arithmetic (flexible parsing, floor/ceiling/round, calendar components, month rollback)
cards.when: date cleaning BEFORE #78 and the other nodes; parsing raw strings into dates and timestamps, calendar rounding, extracting numeric fields, safe month arithmetic with rollback
cards.when_not: layout or frequency plumbing of an already-timed series -> #78; simple day arithmetic -> the standard library; charts (the frontend)

alternatives.criterion: the series ALREADY carries a time index -> layout and frequency plumbing; this card comes first, to build the date column

alternatives.alt: plain date parsing, formatting and arithmetic
alternatives.criterion: homogeneous ISO input with no need for month rollback -> the standard library suffices; this card is for heterogeneous parsing plus month arithmetic with rollback

output_key_fields: dates: parsed/rounded/shifted Date|timestamp -> ISO-8601 strings (+ n, n_na, class)
values: the numeric calendar field (quarter 1-4, wday 1-7,..) from date_component
applied args: order/orders/tz | unit/boundary | component | months/op
interpretation_traps: silent blanks: the parsers return an empty value with ONLY a warning on unparsable input -> the wrapper hard-stops on every non-blank failure (blocked-by-gate)
%m+%/%m-% rollback: 31 Jan %m+% 1 month = 28/29 Feb (NOT an overflow) — the reason it exists; months is built with period(month=n) because months is NOT exported
wday defaults to week_start=7 (Sunday=1); unit is a closed enum {month,quarter,year,week,day}, otherwise a cryptic 'Invalid unit specification'
sources: Grolemund & Wickham 2011 JSS 40(3) (dates and times made easy)

cards.method: Business-day calendar + working-day arithmetic (calendar creation / business-day count / offset / adjust / sequence) from a closed specification (holidays + weekdays)
cards.when: BUSINESS-day arithmetic on a calendar built from a closed specification; T+n settlement, NETWORKDAYS counting, rolling to a business day, enumerating business days; fixed income/derivatives
cards.when_not: series layout or frequency conversion -> #78; fractional business days; the market calendars shipped by third parties; imputation or aggregation

alternatives.criterion: Excel NETWORKDAYS: the count must start/end on a business day
inclusive counting (it also counts the final business day; +1 against financial=True)
the market roll convention (following vs preceding)
you need a time-series transformation, not calendar arithmetic

output_key_fields: bday_create_calendar: weekdays/financial/adjust_from/adjust_to + n_holidays/holidays + start_date/end_date + n_bizdays (a validation summary; NOT the raw Calendar object)
bday_count: count (integer vector, NETWORKDAYS-style) + from/to (Date->ISO) + n + financial
bday_offset: result (shifted Date->ISO) + dates + n + n_out
bday_adjust: result (rolled Date->ISO) + dates + direction + n_out
bday_sequence: sequence (business days, Date->ISO) + n + from/to
interpretation_traps: weekdays: only the 7 LOWER-CASE English tokens; 'Saturday'/'funday' SILENTLY become business days (silently wrong) -> hard gate
bday_offset: a fractional n returns nothing SILENTLY -> a gate on integers
financial=True (the default) does NOT count the final business day; it gives one less than financial=False
the default range = [min,max] of the holidays; dates outside it error with 'Given date out of range' -> widen start_date/end_date
from>to: bday_count returns a NEGATIVE value and bday_sequence a cryptic error -> a gate on from<=to
sources: ISO 8601 and the standard business-day conventions (following / modified following / preceding)
2006 ISDA Definitions — business-day/day-count conventions (following/preceding/modified following, NETWORKDAYS)

cards.method: Tidy temporal data frames — an explicit key/index contract + structural gap handling (detect/list/count/fill) + CLOSED-vocabulary calendar aggregation
cards.when: a long frame -> a contract-checked temporal table with an explicit index (and an optional key); detecting and materialising implicit gaps; calendar aggregation to a lower frequency; it feeds #8 and #126
cards.when_not: free-form expressions (excluded); layout-agnostic conversion -> #78; statistical imputation -> #80 (tt_fill_gaps only inserts the empty rows); INCREASING the frequency -> #79; charts (the frontend)

alternatives.criterion: class-agnostic conversion/transformation without the key/index contract (lighter)
calendar buckets per key here, against plain layout-agnostic aggregation in #78

output_key_fields: series: tbl_ts (to_mcp -> records; a calendar index -> strings 'YYYY QN'/'YYYY Mon') — the main PRODUCER result
class/n/index/key/measured/interval: compact metadata + the applied arguments
tt_gaps: result + any_gaps + n_missing (has=keys with gaps; scan=the missing rows; count=the sum of n)
tt_fill_gaps: n_filled (the rows added, left empty)
interpretation_traps: a raw Date index on monthly/quarterly data -> interval=1D (the GCD of the days) -> SPURIOUS gaps; supply yearmonth/yearquarter; the interval is returned explicitly
tt_index_aggregate with a key SILENTLY merges the keys together; by_key=True (the default) aggregates per key instead
coarsening to a HIGHER resolution than the index (finer than the source) => a clean error (caught), not a silent one
the reducers apply only to NUMERIC measured columns (gated before the cryptic summarise error)
sources: Wang, Cook & Hyndman (2020), A New Tidy Data Structure to Support Exploration and Modeling of Temporal Data, JCGS 29(3):466-478, doi:10.1080/10618600.2019.1695624

cards.method: Robust outlier handling + robust measures of location/scale (winsorize/trim/robust-z/Huber-M)
cards.when: cleaning the tails BEFORE an econometric method; capping/trimming extreme values, robust median/MAD z-scores, Huber-M location (+ a Wald CI); macro series with spikes/crises
cards.when_not: rolling or time-varying cleaning -> #110/#109; imputation -> #80; robust or quantile regression -> #64; matrix or frame input (a vector only)

alternatives.criterion: without outliers -> mean/sd is more efficient; with outliers -> rob_zscore (median/MAD)
winsorize keeps n (capping); trim reduces n (dropping)

output_key_fields: rob_winsorize: values/lower/upper/probs/n_changed
rob_trim: values/trimmed_indices/n_trimmed/trimmed_mean; rob_zscore: values/center(median)/scale(MAD)
rob_huber: location/lower/upper/conf_level (blank when no interval was requested)
interpretation_traps: Winsorize has no probs argument — the wrapper computes val=quantile(x,probs) first (a convenience layer)
rob_zscore has no gap-dropping option, so a gap silently blanks everything (hard gate); scaling with MAD=0 gives all NaN (hard gate)
trim ∈ [0,0.5); >=0.5 blanks silently; a gap with na_rm=False blanks silently (all gated)
sources: Huber (1964), Robust Estimation of a Location Parameter

cards.method: Benchmarking a high-frequency indicator to a low-frequency total (two-step Prais-Winsten regression + additive Denton smoothing)
cards.when: a high-frequency indicator is bent so that it sums EXACTLY to a low-frequency target total (the INSEE two-step: Prais-Winsten GLS + additive Denton); annualBenchmark = the default QNA windows
cards.when_not: a broad menu of disaggregation methods (Chow-Lin/Fernandez/Litterman/Denton-Cholette) -> #79; plain aggregation with no consistency constraint -> ts_aggregate (#78); proportional three-rule smoothing (omitted); charts (the frontend)

alternatives.criterion: you want an explicit choice of disaggregation model (chow-lin/fernandez/litterman/denton) or high->low aggregation (ta)
annual->sub-annual with the usual default windows of quarterly national accounts

output_key_fields: benchmarked: the high-frequency series (->{values,start,frequency}) — the MAIN result; = fitted_values + smoothed_part; it sums exactly to lfserie within the window
coefficients/std_errors/rho: the Prais-Winsten regression (constant + the loading on the indicator); rho=0 = no AR term (not a failure)
fitted_values/smoothed_part: the two additive components (ts); n_high/freq_high/freq_low/freq_ratio metadata
model: the fitted twoStepsBenchmark handle (RDS bucket) -> bench_in_sample / coef / se / rho
comparison (bench_in_sample): a two-column frame (benchmark against predicted value), type changes|levels
interpretation_traps: FREQUENCY GATE: the high-frequency series must be STRICTLY faster than the low-frequency one, at an integer ratio; an equal frequency (ratio 1) would be accepted SILENTLY and is degenerate -> hard-blocked
a gap in the low-frequency series silently blanks the coefficients and the benchmark (silently wrong) -> hard-blocked
include_differenciation=1 (a number) would be accepted silently as True -> a strict boolean gate
consistency holds ONLY inside the benchmark window; the extrapolation tail (hf beyond lf) is a projection, not a benchmarked value
sources: Denton 1971, Adjustment of Series to Annual Totals (JASA 66(333):99-102); Prais & Winsten 1954; INSEE/Banque de France two-step benchmarking

cards.method: Fast row/column panel statistics (median/var/sd/quantiles) + a diffusion index (breadth) over a numeric wide panel matrix
cards.when: a wide numeric panel (matrix rows=time, cols=series); fast cross-sectional (per-period) & over-time (per-series) location/spread, quantiles per period (fan chart), and a diffusion index (the share of series that rise)
cards.when_not: a single series or layout handling -> #78; rolling windows -> #105; ACF/PACF/correlation -> #81; grouped or panel-aware work with ids -> #103; it accepts ONLY a plain numeric matrix

alternatives.criterion: grouped/panel-aware aggregation with ids, or speed on very large data
class/frequency plumbing of one or a few series rather than cross-sectional panel statistics

output_key_fields: values: a numeric vector (by row -> n_time cross-sectional, by column -> n_series over time) + margin/stat/na_rm
quantiles: a matrix n_time x len(probs), columns named by prob (drop=False keeps a matrix for a single prob)
index: the diffusion index of length n_time-1 in [0,1] (0.5=balance, >0.5=broad expansion)
interpretation_traps: na_rm=False => a gap PROPAGATES (visible, NOT a silent drop); set it True to ignore gaps
row = per-period cross-sectional; col = per-series over time — do not confuse the axis
a time-indexed object also answers to the matrix check and would be accepted silently -> a hard gate blocks it; supply a plain numeric matrix
a row variance or standard deviation over a single element is blank (the variance of one value), not an error
sources: diffusion index / breadth as a leading indicator: Stock & Watson 'Diffusion Indexes'; Conference Board business-cycle diffusion methodology

cards.method: Composite index / dimensionality reduction with PCA (PC1 composite index + loadings + variance decomposition + biplot coordinates + newdata projection + rules for the number of components + KPSS precheck)
cards.when: many correlated indicators -> ONE composite index = PC1 (data-driven loadings); dimensionality reduction; cum_var for the number of components; scale=True (default) for heterogeneous units; biplot chart-data (observation scores + variable arrows in the SAME scaled space) -> pca_biplot_coords; out-of-sample apply: fit on train, project NEW rows with the SAME center/scale -> pca_predict; how many components to keep BY A RULE (Kaiser-Guttman / cum-var / broken-stick) -> pca_n_components; BEFORE PCA on TIME SERIES: KPSS per column -> pca_stationarity_precheck
cards.when_not: charts as DRAWING (the frontend; we supply ONLY coordinates); a latent factor with dynamics, mixed frequency or missing data -> #15 (category 03); explicit or equal weights -> panel_row_stats (#116) / #82; NON-STATIONARY series in LEVELS -> #256 (pn_pca_nonstationary); the elbow or scree plot as a rule (Cattell 1966: it requires VISUAL judgement, not a rule)

alternatives.criterion: a common latent factor with dynamics/mixed frequency/gaps (state space) rather than a static cross-section
you want explicit/audited (equal/expert) weights instead of data-driven loadings
a measurement model with error terms (factor analysis), not maximisation of explained variance
the columns are NON-STATIONARY time series (KPSS rejects) — the standardization of classical PCA is MATHEMATICALLY UNDEFINED there (Hamilton, Ma & Xi, NBER WP 32068)

output_key_fields: composite: PC1 scores = the composite index (numeric of length n, names from row labels)
loadings/scores: matrices (p x k / n x k) -> nested rows + axis labels
var_explained/cum_var: the share & cumulative share per PC1/PC2/..; pc1_var = the share of the composite
sdev, n_obs/n_vars/n_comp, center/scale (the applied arguments)
pca_biplot_coords: obs_coords (n x 2) / var_coords (p x 2) / lambda (the COMMON scale factor) / components / var_explained — NUMBERS ONLY, no drawing (charter §5)

pca_predict: scores_new / composite_new / rotation / center_used / scale_used (fit/apply externalization — a reproducible apply OUTSIDE the node: scale(new, center_used, scale_used) %*% rotation) / scores_train
pca_n_components: k_kaiser + kaiser_threshold + kaiser_basis · k_cum_var + cum_var_threshold · k_broken_stick (sequential) + k_broken_stick_any + broken_stick_expected · k_min/k_max

pca_stationarity_precheck: statistic/p_value/p_at_bound/trunc_lag/nonstationary PER COLUMN · columns_flagged/n_nonstationary/any_nonstationary/small_sample · warning_code/warning_message/recommended_node/recommended_fn/source (a STRUCTURED field, NOT message, NOT stop)
interpretation_traps: PC signs are arbitrary (help Note, they differ by build/BLAS) -> an explicit sign normalization: each PC is flipped so that the max-|loading| is positive; interpret the direction from the loadings
scale=True is a hard gate against a constant or zero-variance column (otherwise 'cannot rescale a constant/zero column'); a gap or an infinity gives a cryptic decomposition error
PC1 is z-score-like (mean ~ 0) with no natural units -> for a base-100 index do a separate rebase; scale=False lets the highest-variance column dominate
the input must be a numeric matrix (NOT a data_frame -> silent character coercion), >=2 columns, >=3 rows

pca_predict matches columns BY NAME only when the rotation carries them — that is, when the training matrix had column names. Without them only the column COUNT is checked, and reordered columns project SILENTLY WRONG (live-verified: the same input, completely different scores) ⇒ pca_predict requires column names on BOTH sides AND an identical ORDER
biplot_scale is NOT the PCA scaling flag: it is the lambda exponent of the biplot. The reference construction only WARNS outside [0,1]; here it is a hard stop (charter §5)

a biplot on a rank-deficient matrix (a duplicate or collinear column): sdev ~ 1.18e-16, NOT exactly 0 -> lam ~ 0 -> silently enormous observation coordinates. Gated with the documented tolerance of the decomposition: sqrt(machine epsilon) * sdev[0]

the Kaiser-Guttman «eigenvalue > 1» rule HOLDS ONLY on a CORRELATION matrix (scale=True, mean eigenvalue == 1). On a COVARIANCE matrix (scale=False) the threshold is the mean of the eigenvalues (Jolliffe 2002 §6.1.2) — which is why kaiser_threshold and kaiser_basis are returned explicitly

broken-stick: «ALL of them pass» is MATHEMATICALLY IMPOSSIBLE (sum(var_explained) == sum(b_j) == 1); k_broken_stick (which stops at the FIRST failure) and k_broken_stick_any DIFFER (e.g. on ~independent columns: k=0 but k_any=2)
kpss_test gives a p-value ONLY within [0.01, 0.10] (interpolation in KPSS 1992 Table 1) and warns at the bounds ⇒ alpha is gated to [0.01, 0.10] + p_at_bound per column
non-stationarity is NOT a stop: the node must stay fully usable on CROSS-SECTION data (countries/firms), where stationarity is not even defined — hence a STRUCTURED warning is returned
sources: Venables & Ripley, Modern Applied Statistics with S (2002); Jolliffe, Principal Component Analysis (2002) §6.1.1/§6.1.2
OECD/JRC Nardo et al., Handbook on Constructing Composite Indicators (2008) — PCA weighting
the biplot construction (lam = (sdev*sqrt(n))^scale; observations divided by lam, variables multiplied by it) · Gabriel 1971 Biometrika 58(3):453-467
Kaiser HF (1960), Educ. Psychol. Meas. 20:141-151 · Guttman L (1954) — eigenvalue>1 on a correlation matrix
Frontier 1976 · Jackson 1993 Ecology 74(8):2204-2214 — the broken stick, b_j = (1/p) * sum over i from j to p of 1/i
Cattell RB (1966) — elbow/scree is REJECTED as a rule (it requires visual judgement, not a rule)
Hamilton, Ma & Xi, NBER WP 32068 — for a non-stationary variable the population mean is undefined and the sample sd diverges ⇒ PCA standardization is invalid

Kwiatkowski, Phillips, Schmidt & Shin 1992, J. Econometrics 54:159-178 · the kpss_test routine (lshort=True ⇒ a truncation lag of floor(4*(n/100)^0.25); Table 1 ⇒ small_sample = n<30; a p-value only within [0.01,0.10])
precondition_tools: pca_stationarity_precheck # ONLY when the input is TIME SERIES (in a cross-section stationarity is undefined)

cards.method: Parametric distributions (normal/student_t) as a numeric grid: quantile bands / cdf / density / moments (fan-chart data)
cards.when: a forecast/scenario from PARAMETERS (mean/sd, df) -> numeric data for the frontend: fan bands per horizon, CDF/tail probability, a density curve, moments
cards.when_not: density-forecast scoring (CRPS/LogS/PIT) -> #94; empirical quantiles from a sample -> #110; FITTING a distribution to data -> #196 (this card takes parameters, it does not fit); charts -> the frontend

alternatives.criterion: density-forecast EVALUATION (CRPS/LogS/PIT) rather than grid generation
fat tails in the scenario -> student_t (a small df); otherwise normal (df->inf)

output_key_fields: dist_fan_quantiles: quantiles (matrix n_dist x n_probs) + probs/family/params + mean/sd
dist_prob_cdf: cdf (n_dist x n_at) in [0,1]; dist_density_grid: density (n_dist x n_at) >=0
dist_moments: mean/variance/sd per distribution
interpretation_traps: probs must be strictly in (0,1): probs>1 => a silent WARN 'NaNs produced' (silently wrong); 0/1 => ±Inf (hard gate)
Student-t: the variance is infinite for df<=2, the mean is undefined for df<=1 => to_mcp null (NOT 0)
sigma is a scale, NOT the sd for a t: sd = sigma*sqrt(df/(df-2)) for df>2; recycling of length 1 or L (otherwise a clean stop)
sources: distributional reference/pkgdown (dist_normal/dist_student_t/cdf/variance; generics quantile/density) v0.8.1
O'Hara-Wild et al., distributional: Vectorised Probability Distributions

cards.method: US NBER recession chronology — recession-shading intervals + a per-date 0/1 recession dummy
cards.when: the official NBER peak->trough recession intervals as numeric data -> recession-shading bands (frontend) or a 0/1 recession-dummy regressor aligned to a series
cards.when_not: DRAWING the bands (nberShade/ymdShade/romerLines — frontend); DATING turning points from data — these two functions date nothing, they clip and test intervals the caller already has, so a chronology has to exist before either is called; Romer dates (not exposed)

alternatives.criterion: you need the series itself/transformations, not a recession reference
you want a 0/1 dummy per date rather than intervals for shading

output_key_fields: recessions: records df start/end = peak->trough (yyyymmdd int by default, or Date); overlap-clipped to [from,to]
flags: records df date/in_recession 0/1 + n_recession_periods
metadata: n_recessions/n, from/to (yyyymmdd), as_date

vintage: n_intervals + the first and last date read off the chronology THAT ARRIVED — the engine holds no snapshot to describe, so this echoes the caller's input rather than a publisher, a retrieval date or a digest of anything shipped
interpretation_traps: the window is INCLUSIVE at both ends (Start=peak & End=trough are inside the recession); the day after the trough => 0
a recession-free [from,to] => 0 rows (valid, NOT an error)
20200101 is a yyyymmdd INTEGER, NOT a year; from=2020 errors (not an 8-digit date)

the committee dates peaks and troughs to a MONTH, and separately to a QUARTER — it publishes no day. Every day-of-month in a redistributed recession dataset was chosen by whoever repackaged it, not by the NBER, so two chronologies claiming the same recession can disagree on its edges by up to a month. These functions take dates at day precision because their windows and their output are day-precision; that is a convention of the argument, never a claim that the underlying date is known to the day

the answer is only ever as good as the chronology handed in: supply a different one and every interval, flag and count moves with it. Nothing here validates the chronology against the committee's, because nothing here has the committee's to compare against
sources: NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee — US business cycle expansions and contractions (nber.org). Where a caller GETS a chronology, not something this engine ships or retrieves; the committee's own notice grants copying provided the source is attributed, so attribution is the form that use takes

cards.method: Numeric rescaling (min-max / around-mid) + axis break positions (extended/log) + label strings (number/percent)
cards.when: a DATA helper: linear rescaling of a series to a target range, computing axis-break positions as DATA (Wilkinson/log), formatting numbers into number/percent label strings
cards.when_not: macro-semantic rebase/deflate/per-capita -> macro-arithmetic #82 / ts_rebase #78; chart/colour palettes/plot scale objects -> frontend; z-score standardization -> ts_standardize #78

alternatives.criterion: you want a z-score (mean/sd) rather than a min-max range rescale
you want a date-anchored base=100 index with economic meaning rather than a mechanical [0,1]

output_key_fields: values: the rescaled numbers (the same length as x, gaps preserved) + to/from/mid/n
breaks: numeric axis positions (round numbers, n_breaks~n, NOT exactly n) + n_breaks/type/base
labels: character label strings (percent = x100 + '%') + type/n
interpretation_traps: to/from MUST be numeric of length 2; length 1 => zero_range => mean(to) for EVERY element (silently wrong, gated)
n>=1 integer (n<=0 => extended loops forever); base>1 (base<=1 => breaks_log loops forever); type='log' requires positive values
scale_rescale is a min-max range rescale (NOT a z-score, NOT a base=100 index); a constant series => mean(to)
sources: Talbot, Lin & Hanrahan 2010 IEEE TVCG 16(6) (an extension of Wilkinson's algorithm for optimal axis labeling)

cards.method: Analytic OLS on a CLOSED formula: a deterministic time trend (linear/quadratic) + the detrended series, or response ~ named numeric predictor columns
cards.when: a fast deterministic (analytic QR, no seed) linear model in the data layer: removing a deterministic trend (ols_trend->detrended) or a simple regression on explicitly named numeric columns (ols_regress); the formula is ALWAYS closed (an enum or bare names) through reformulate
cards.when_not: charts (the frontend); a stochastic trend or unit root -> differencing and the unit-root tests of #2 (not a deterministic detrend, which would be spurious); categorical terms, interactions, weighted least squares or an offset (a numeric-only closed design); residual diagnostics -> pass the model handle to #76/#77

alternatives.criterion: explicit macro conventions (growth/deflate/rebase) rather than a model
a flexible/non-parametric trend rather than a low-order polynomial
the question is detrending vs differencing (trend- vs difference-stationary)

output_key_fields: coefficients: long-format -> term/estimate/std_error/statistic(t)/p_value (records)
glance: glance -> r_squared/adj_r_squared/sigma/AIC/BIC/log_lik/df_residual/nobs
fitted/residuals: numeric vectors; ols_trend adds detrended (=the trend residuals); n/k observations/parameters
model: the fitted lm — a producer handle (RDS bucket) for diagnostics/prediction nodes

cards.method: CORRELATION FILTER: greedy removal of highly correlated variables (over a VALIDATED correlation matrix) + an out-of-sample APPLY with the fitted column names
cards.when: PRE-PROCESSING before a high-dimensional/collinearity-sensitive model (regression, PCA, ML): on an observations x variables matrix (countries x indicators, periods x variables) you drop AS MANY COLUMNS as needed so that NO remaining pairwise |r| exceeds the cutoff; the rule: for every pair above the threshold, the variable with the LARGEST MEAN |correlation| with ALL the others (= the most redundant overall) is deleted; the flow: cf_cor_matrix (a VALIDATED p x p matrix) -> cf_find_correlation (WHICH ones go) -> cf_filter (fit + apply)
cards.when_not: TIME SERIES IN I(1) LEVELS (spurious correlation — supply DIFFERENCES EXPLICITLY; there is NEVER an implicit differencing here); a SIGNIFICANCE test for a correlation, with p-values, intervals and multiplicity -> #81 desc_cor_test; DISTANCES, clustering or MDS, where the object is a distance built from 1 minus the correlation -> #240 dm_correlation_distance (category 29); dimension COMPRESSION rather than SELECTION, keeping all the information in a few axes -> #117; exact LINEAR COMBINATIONS of dependence, found by a QR decomposition — NOT exposed; stateful preprocessing pipelines (EXPLICITLY REJECTED, the normative gate spec §3b); charts and heatmaps (the frontend, §5); p = 1, since at least two variables are required

alternatives.criterion: ALWAYS, unless p is very large: it recomputes the mean correlations at EVERY step and removes FEWER variables («The exact calculations will remove a smaller number of predictors but can be much slower», the findCorrelation routine Details)

ONLY when p is so large that the exact path is prohibitively slow; an EXPLICIT choice — the two paths give DIFFERENT sets (live on the help-page R1, cutoff 0.6: exact -> {x1,x4,x5}; fast -> {x1,x3,x4,x5})
the relation is MONOTONE but not linear, or outliers are present (rank-based, robust); kendall is O(n^2) and is slow at large n; the default pearson = a LINEAR relation

NEW data (test/out-of-sample): it applies THE SAME filter WITHOUT re-estimation (§3b gate 6); CRITICAL — a re-fit on the test set changes the COLUMN SET and the model breaks (live-verified in the tests: a different sample -> a different filter)
you want COMPRESSION (all the variables contribute to a few orthogonal axes) rather than the SELECTION of a subset of columns; the filter keeps INTERPRETABLE original variables, PCA does not
the smaller the cutoff, the more columns leave; read max_abs_offdiag/n_pairs_above_before from cf_cor_matrix first — if max|r| < cutoff NOTHING leaves

output_key_fields: cf_cor_matrix: cor (a p x p VALIDATED matrix — heatmap chart-data) + method/use('everything', PINNED) + n/p/variables + mean_abs_cor (THE greedy criterion, per variable) + max_abs_offdiag/max_abs_pair/max_abs_index + min_cor/max_cor/n_pairs + eigen_min/is_psd (a PSD DIAGNOSTIC, NOT a gate)
cf_find_correlation: remove_index/remove_names AND keep_index/keep_names (= the FITTED PARAMS, §3b gate 6; ALWAYS sorted ascending) + n_variables/n_removed/n_kept/share_removed

cf_find_correlation: max_abs_before vs max_abs_after (+ max_abs_pair_before/after) and n_pairs_above_before vs n_pairs_above_after (ALWAYS 0 — the algorithm's invariant) — the main «before/after» chart-data

cf_filter: data (THE FILTERED DATA, n x n_variables_out — it becomes a handle: the card's SOLE producer/register) + mode ('fit' | 'apply') + keep_names/remove_names + n_variables_in/out + n/cutoff/exact/method/variables
cf_filter in mode='apply': cor and mean_abs_cor are absent, and max_abs_before and max_abs_after blank — DOCUMENTED, and meaning «NO re-estimation»: it is a pure column subselection
interpretation_traps: DETERMINISM #1 (§5): the documented upstream default makes the exact path conditional on having fewer than 100 columns — THE ALGORITHM CHANGES AT 100 COLUMNS. A node that changed path because the user added the hundredth variable would be NON-REPRODUCIBLE ⇒ 'exact' is an EXPLICIT argument with OUR OWN constant default of True, never the upstream one

DETERMINISM #2: the ORDER in which the selector returns its indices depends on the column order (live: the same SET, in a different ORDER, once the columns are reversed) ⇒ CANONICALIZATION, so the indices and names always come back in ascending order. There is no randomness anywhere, and no seed; two identical runs are pinned in the tests, for both the wrapper and the node path

SILENTLY WRONG (the main reason this wrapper exists): the selector REQUIRES A CORRELATION MATRIX, yet with exact=False it SILENTLY accepts RAW DATA (live: a 10x5 random matrix returned «2 3 1» as though those were correlations); ONLY the exact path checks symmetry ⇒ OUR OWN symmetry, diagonal and range checks run ALWAYS, on both paths

SILENTLY WRONG: a non-square 3x4 matrix with exact=False returns an EMPTY selection SILENTLY; p=1 with exact=False does the same, while the exact path at least says «only one variable given»; a diagonal other than 1, and correlations outside [-1,1], pass SILENTLY on BOTH paths — that is, ANYTHING symmetric is accepted as a «correlation» (did you supply a COVARIANCE matrix? convert it first)

SILENTLY WRONG: a CONSTANT, zero-variance column makes the correlation emit ONLY the warning «the standard deviation is zero» and blank the WHOLE row and column (live-verified in the engine); the selector then fails cryptically — «The correlation matrix has some missing values», or a bare type error on the exact path ⇒ a hard gate that NAMES the constant columns

SILENTLY WRONG: a correlation on a single observation returns an ENTIRELY blank matrix WITHOUT even a warning; on two observations every correlation is 1 in absolute value BY DEFINITION, since two points define a line ⇒ a hard gate of n >= 3 in the FIT, while in the APPLY step n >= 1 suffices, because the names are GIVEN rather than estimated
SILENTLY WRONG: a cutoff of 1.5 selects NOTHING silently, so nothing is filtered, while a cutoff at or below 0 removes almost EVERYTHING. The selector does NOT check ⇒ a hard gate, 0 < cutoff < 1

§3b GATE 6 (fit/apply externalization): keep_names/remove_names ARE the fitted params and are ALWAYS returned; cf_filter(keep=..) applies them to NEW data WITHOUT re-estimation. If the filter is re-estimated on the test set, the COLUMN SET CHANGES (different correlations) and the trained model's coefficients are applied to the WRONG columns (the KNIME «Normalize Model» pattern). That is also why duplicate column labels are a hard gate: the apply would be ambiguous

§3b GATE 3 (non-stationarity): the node is CROSS-SECTION/PANEL. In I(1) LEVELS the sample correlation does NOT converge to a population parameter (spurious correlation, Granger-Newbold 1974; Hamilton-Ma-Xi for why the standardization is undefined) => supply DIFFERENCES EXPLICITLY upstream; NEVER an implicit differencing here
§3b GATE 2 (no implicit standardization): correlation is INVARIANT to linear transformations => there is NO scale/center argument (it would be a no-op implying a non-existent option)

PSD: A DOCUMENTED DEVIATION — a non-positive-semidefinite matrix is exposed as eigen_min/is_psd but does NOT block: the greedy algorithm stays well defined (it compares |r| per pair) and it is LIVE-VERIFIED that EVEN the R1 matrix in the reference documentation itself has a minimum eigenvalue of -0.2634288 (the same holds for published matrices rounded to 2 decimals)

PINNED ARGUMENTS: the verbose switch is off, since turning it on PRINTS («Compare row 1 and column 5 with corr 0.85...»), a violation of §5; the names switch is off, since the documented return value is INVERTED against the live behaviour — we supply BOTH the indices AND the names ourselves; and the correlation is PINNED to complete data, because pairwise completion computes EVERY pair on a DIFFERENT sample and can yield a matrix that is not positive semi-definite, and an inconsistent filter

THE BOUNDARY against #240 (dm_correlation_distance, category 29): there a DISTANCE object, 1 minus the correlation, is produced for clustering — a DIFFERENT object with DIFFERENT semantics, since 1-r reverses the direction and loses the sign, and it does NOT feed the selector here. cf_cor_matrix exists ONLY so that this node is usable end to end

cards.method: DESIGN MATRIX (feature engineering): ORTHOGONAL/RAW polynomials (returning the fitted coefficients), INTERACTIONS without a formula surface, an allowlisted formula path, a COMBINATORIAL factor
cards.when: IMMEDIATELY BEFORE any regression/ML node, when you need NON-LINEARITY (polynomials: the Phillips curve, threshold-like relations) or INTERACTIONS (a*b, regime x variable, country x sector): the node builds the DESIGN MATRIX EXPLICITLY, GATED and — most critically — REPRODUCIBLY OUT OF SAMPLE (it returns AND accepts back the fitted params: coefs_alpha/coefs_norm2 · xlev + contrasts + column_names)
cards.when_not: model ESTIMATION — the node does NOT run a regression, it supplies ONLY the matrix X, and the dependent variable does not belong here, since the formula is ONE-SIDED; spline or semi-parametric bases (ANOTHER family, with its own card); DISCRETISATION of a continuous variable into categories -> #255; calendar dummies -> #254 hd_dummies; filtering of collinear columns -> #252 cf_filter; sparse matrices (a new dependency); stateful preprocessing pipelines (REJECTED, the normative gate spec §3b); charts (the frontend, §5)

alternatives.criterion: you want main terms + all interactions up to 'order' from VALIDATED COLUMN NAMES: NO formula comes from the user — the RCE surface DOES NOT EVEN EXIST (the formula is built internally from language objects; ZERO parse/eval)

you GENUINELY need an expression that cannot be stated with names+order: I(x^2), log(x), nested factors, an explicit removal of terms; it passes TWICE through a default-deny allowlist (adapt_formula at L3 + an independent walk in the wrapper) and NEVER accepts a string

you want INTERPRETABLE coefficients on the original scale (x, x², x³); the price is SEVERE collinearity, and the p-values of the lower degrees CHANGE when a higher one is added. The default, False, gives an ORTHOGONAL basis: numerically stable, with uncorrelated columns
NEW data: MANDATORY in order to produce THE SAME basis — a re-fit poly on the new data gives A DIFFERENT BASIS and the trained model's coefficients mean nothing (§3b gate 6)
NEW data with factors: MANDATORY — with FEWER levels in newdata model_matrix produces SILENTLY FEWER COLUMNS (live-verified) and the coefficients land in the WRONG POSITIONS

alternatives.alt: the sum-to-zero contrast instead of the treatment contrast
alternatives.criterion: you want the interactions interpretable as DEVIATIONS FROM THE MEAN, so that the main term stops meaning «relative to the first level»; the Helmert contrast gives successive contrasts, and the polynomial contrast orthogonal polynomials for ORDERED categories
you want ONE COMBINATORIAL FACTOR (e.g. country x regime as A SINGLE categorical column for fixed effects/grouping) instead of column products in a design matrix

the DOWNSTREAM node is regularized (ridge/lasso, cat 20) and rank deficiency is not an error; 'auto' (the default) is STRICT ('stop') in the FIT and TOLERANT ('report') in the APPLY, where an absent level is NORMAL

output_key_fields: ply_polynomial: basis (n x degree — chart data) + column_names (the base name with a degree suffix) + degree and raw + coefs_alpha (of length degree), coefs_norm2 (of length degree+2) and coefs_source ('fitted', 'supplied' or 'raw'), which are THE FITTED PARAMETERS (§3b gate 6), + orthonormality_error and centering_error (ONLY on the fit path) + n/n_unique/x_min/x_max/name

ply_interactions & ply_model_matrix: design (an n x k BARE numeric matrix) + column_names/n_columns/n_rows + column_term & assign (COLUMN -> TERM; 0 = intercept) + term_labels/n_terms/intercept + formula (deparsed)

ply_interactions & ply_model_matrix: xlev (THE LEVELS PER FACTOR) + xlev_source ('fitted'|'supplied') + contrasts/contrasts_arg + variables/factor_vars/numeric_vars = THE design matrix's FITTED PARAMS (§3b gate 6)

ply_interactions & ply_model_matrix: rank + rank_deficient + rank_check/rank_check_arg + column_bound (THE UPPER BOUND checked BEFORE construction) + max_columns/max_levels; ply_interactions additionally order/include_main/built_formula

ply_interaction_categorical: levels + codes (1 to n_levels per row) + counts (chart data) + n_levels/n_used_levels + empty_levels/n_empty_levels/has_empty_levels + indicator, an n x n_levels 0/1 matrix when it was requested, + input_levels (fit and apply) + combinations/drop/sep/lex_order/n
interpretation_traps: §3b GATE 6 — THE NODE'S REASON FOR EXISTING: an ORTHOGONAL polynomial is NOT a function of x alone — it depends on the CENTRES and NORMS (alpha, norm2) computed ON THE TRAINING SAMPLE. Re-fitting the basis on new data would give A DIFFERENT BASIS, and the model's coefficients would then mean nothing. That is why the coefficients are returned AS NUMBERS and accepted back (the KNIME Normalizer «Normalize Model» pattern); the simplified basis DISCARDS them — live, only the shape attributes survive — which is why it is NOT exposed

§3b GATE 6 (b) — A SILENTLY WRONG BEHAVIOUR OF model_matrix: newdata with FEWER factor levels produces FEWER COLUMNS WITHOUT ANY ERROR (live-verified: ~a*g with 3 levels -> (Intercept),a,gy,gz,a:gy,a:gz; the same newdata with 2 levels -> (Intercept),a,gy,a:gy) => the coefficients are applied at the WRONG POSITIONS. That is why xlev + expect_columns are returned/accepted, with a hard gate on an UNKNOWN level («factor a has new level..») AND on a different column set

SECURITY (the project's security rule — NEVER evaluate a user string): ply_interactions EXPOSES NO formula surface; it builds the right-hand side symbolically over names that (a) really exist in the data and (b) pass a strict identifier pattern, then implants it into a TEMPLATE formula whose environment is sealed to the base one ⇒ there is ZERO path from a string to a parse or an evaluation

SECURITY (ply_model_matrix, THREE LAYERS OF DEFENCE): (1) at tier 3 the string passes ONLY through the formula adapter — a default-deny allowlist walk with no evaluation, inside a sealed enclosure; (2) the wrapper does NOT accept a string AT ALL, only an already-parsed formula object; (3) an INDEPENDENT default-deny allowlist walk that runs even in isolation and ADDITIONALLY restricts EVERY symbol to the data's column names. ONLY these are allowed: the formula and arithmetic operators ~ + - * : ^ ( ), the identity wrapper, the logarithms and the exponential, the square root and the absolute value, the polynomial basis, the categorical constructors, and the interaction constructor; the dot shorthand is explicitly rejected; the expression depth is capped at 64; and the head of every call MUST be a plain symbol

SILENTLY WRONG (the polynomial basis): a FRACTIONAL degree does NOT error — it is SILENTLY truncated downwards (live, a degree of 1.5 gave one column); coefficients of the WRONG LENGTH give a column FULL OF BLANKS with no error, hence the gate that alpha has exactly `degree` entries and norm2 exactly `degree+2` (live-verified: degree 3 gives 3 and 5); coefficients supplied TOGETHER WITH raw=True are SILENTLY ignored; and once the degree reaches the number of unique values the ORTHOGONAL basis errors («'degree' must be less than number of unique points») while the RAW one does NOT — it simply produces LINEARLY DEPENDENT columns ⇒ THE SAME gate on both paths

SILENTLY WRONG (gaps): building the model frame SILENTLY DROPS the incomplete rows (live, 6 became 5) and the design matrix CEASES to line up with y ⇒ the missing-value policy is PINNED to fail, plus OUR OWN explicit gap-and-infinity gate BEFORE the call, on the columns actually used only; and dropping unused levels is PINNED off, since enabling it would nullify the recorded level sets

SILENTLY WRONG (RANK DEFICIENCY): empty level combinations produce aliased columns — live-verified, a rank of 2 over 4 columns WITHOUT any error, and a least-squares fit on such a matrix returns blank coefficients silently. The node ALWAYS computes the rank and blocks according to rank_check ('auto' stops in the FIT and reports in the APPLY)

SILENTLY WRONG (the interaction constructor): it accepts a NUMERIC column WITHOUT COMPLAINT and creates ONE LEVEL PER UNIQUE VALUE ⇒ a hard gate, so discretise first (#255); with dropping off, the documented default, the EMPTY levels REMAIN and are reported explicitly in empty_levels, but indicator=True IS BLOCKED whenever empty levels exist, since each one gives a column FULL OF ZEROS, hence rank deficiency and silently blank coefficients

DIMENSION EXPLOSION: an UPPER BOUND on the column count is checked BEFORE the matrix is built — the product of the level counts per term, a numeric column counting as 1 ⇒ a giant matrix is NEVER constructed; max_levels defaults to 30 per categorical column and max_columns to 200 (in ply_interaction_categorical max_levels defaults to 200, and the PRODUCT of the level counts is checked BEFORE the call when dropping is off); and a categorical column with ONLY one level, which would give the cryptic «contrasts can be applied only to factors with 2 or more levels», is caught BEFOREHAND

ORTHONORMALITY: it is checked — the largest deviation of X'X from the identity, and the largest column sum — ONLY on the FIT path, since OUT OF SAMPLE IT DOES NOT HOLD BY DESIGN: the basis is orthogonal WITH RESPECT TO THE TRAINING SAMPLE, not to every new x. On the apply path the two fields are blank — EXPECTED, not an error

DETERMINISM (§5): NO RNG path (poly = QR/a three-term recursion; model_matrix/interaction = combinatorial) => NO seed argument; identical over 2 runs is pinned in the tests (the wrapper AND the node path). TERMINAL nodes: no register — the fit/apply is EXPLICIT (the user hands back coefs/xlev/expect_columns)

cards.when: DAILY/WEEKLY macro or financial series with DETERMINISTIC calendar disturbances (national holidays, exchange closures, the MOVING Easter): you produce EXPLICIT exogenous 0/1 dummies (exog_handle) for ARIMA/regression/GARCH; without them the calendar contaminates the residuals and shows up FALSELY as seasonality or ARCH. few observations or few events per holiday -> ONE column 'holiday_any' (1 = any holiday); fewer degrees of freedom, a single common effect. The is_holiday vector is returned ALWAYS, whatever the choice
you want BOTH the per-holiday columns AND the aggregate (e.g. per-holiday in the model, aggregate in the chart)
FINANCIAL daily data: a CLOSED MARKET is a STRUCTURAL GAP (not a missing value); it gives ONE column named after the centre, IN ADDITION to the named holidays
you want ONLY the EXTRAORDINARY closures (e.g. 2001-09-11.14) — shock events, not institutional holidays; 'standard' = only the institutional ones; 'all' (the default) = ALL

a NEW sample, out of sample or the next wave: IDENTICAL columns IN THE SAME ORDER, even if some holiday does not fall inside it, and INDEPENDENTLY of the catalogue version (§3b gate 6). MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE with holidays, calendar and nyse_type
you do not want dummies but a COUNT of business days between dates, date shifting, or the generation of a business-day sequence under a custom calendar

AN ADDITIONAL hard gate: EVERY name is checked against the catalogue listing BEFORE the call, with an explicit message and the nearby names

DETERMINISM (§5): 'year' is MANDATORY — the upstream default is THE CURRENT YEAR FROM THE CLOCK, which is not reproducible. TIME ZONE: the financial centre is PINNED to GMT (live-verified: THE SAME dates under two very different local zones), and neither the zone nor the centre is exposed. There is no randomness, since the computations are purely calendrical; the output is ALWAYS sorted and de-duplicated, and the column order follows the GIVEN argument order; two identical runs are pinned in the tests

SILENTLY WRONG (years): outside [1000, 9999] the date constructor does NOT error — it returns a blank with ONLY the warning «character string is not in a standard unambiguous format», and year 0 and year 10000 both come back blank; the same for a NON-INTEGER year, and for a missing one. OUR OWN HARD gate is [1583, 2200]: the lower bound is the first FULL year of the GREGORIAN calendar, after the reform of 15 October 1582, because the Easter algorithm is GREGORIAN and before 1583 the results would be ANACHRONISTIC
