cards.method: DISCRETISATION (binning) of ONE numeric column: EQUAL-POPULATION bins (sample quantiles, quantile type 7 PINNED) or EQUAL-WIDTH bins (an explicit seq over the range or over a GIVEN fixed domain) + an out-of-sample APPLY of the STORED breaks
cards.when: converting ONE continuous macro variable into DISCRETE REGIMES (regime dummies): «high vs low inflation», «growth quartile», «spread zone», or INTEGER CODES as the input to a categorical node; ONE node PER variable (fan-out from the frontend). BINNING IS FIT + APPLY: the fit LEARNS the boundaries from the sample, bn_apply REUSES them verbatim on a new sample
cards.when_not: NON-STATIONARY I(1) LEVELS with SAMPLE quantiles, where the «quartiles» reflect the POSITION IN TIME rather than an economic regime — supply differences or rates, or use bn_equal_width with EXOGENOUS boundaries; ENDOGENOUS regime detection from the data themselves -> Markov switching or thresholds (category 06), or #244 (category 29); STRUCTURAL CHANGE POINTS in time -> #3 (category 01); MANY columns at once (one node per variable); NON-LINEARITY WITHOUT information loss -> #253 ply_polynomial, since a polynomial discards nothing while binning DOES; ALREADY categorical variables, which need no binning; charts and histograms (the frontend, §5)

alternatives.criterion: you want EQUAL-POPULATION bins (each regime has the same number of observations => the same statistical power per dummy): 3 = terciles, 4 = quartiles, 5 = quintiles, 10 = deciles
you want UNEQUAL bins with an economic meaning («lower tail / centre / upper tail»); it MUST be strictly increasing with the endpoints EXACTLY 0 and 1; it does NOT combine with n_bins
you want EQUAL-WIDTH bins (interpretable value ranges instead of equal population); under a skewed distribution the extreme bins may end up EMPTY — they are reported explicitly in empty_bins

you want COMPARABLE bins across COUNTRIES/SAMPLES or on a NON-STATIONARY series: you supply THEORETICAL, EXOGENOUS boundaries (e.g. around a 2% inflation target) instead of sample ones — THE CORRECT ROUTE when §3b gate 3 forbids sample quantiles

alternatives.alt: bn_apply(breaks = <breaks of a previous fit>) [§3b gate 6]
alternatives.criterion: NEW data (test/out-of-sample/another country): THE SAME boundaries => COMPARABLE regime dummies; a re-fit gives DIFFERENT boundaries and the out-of-sample result is NOT reproduced. Supply the fit's labels/right/include_lowest as well

'na' assigns an EXPLICIT blank code and records it (n_out_of_range, out_of_range_labels), for when you want to KNOW which new values fell outside; 'clamp' assigns them to the EXTREME bin, for regimes defined as «below or above X» — but it DISTORTS the extreme-value information. The default is 'fail' (blocked-by-gate)

EXPLICIT consent when the column has many TIES and two quantiles coincide: the UNIQUE boundaries are kept, the bins become FEWER than requested (n_breaks_dropped) and they no longer carry equal population; the default, False, is a hard stop
you want the 0/1 indicator matrix (n x n_bins) DIRECTLY as regressors; the missing and out-of-range rows come back blank, NOT 0, since a 0 would mean «definitely not in this bin»
you want NON-LINEARITY WITHOUT information loss — binning discards the WITHIN-BIN variance, polynomials do not

output_key_fields: bin (INTEGER codes 1.n_bins per observation, named) + bin_label (character per observation) + labels (the bin NAMES) — NEVER a factor (JSON-safe)
breaks (NUMERIC, n_bins+1 boundaries) = THE FITTED PARAM (§3b gate 6); it is handed back verbatim to bn_apply together with labels/right/include_lowest
counts + share (histogram chart-data) + bin_lower/bin_upper/bin_width (THE BOUNDARIES) + bin_min/bin_max/bin_mean/bin_median (the OBSERVED range INSIDE each bin) + empty_bins/n_empty_bins
dummies: an n x n_bins 0/1 matrix when requested, blank on the unassignable rows, + method ('quantile', 'equal_width' or 'apply') + right and include_lowest
out_of_range + n_out_of_range/out_of_range_index/out_of_range_labels + n_clamped + n_assigned + n/n_valid/n_missing/missing_index/n_distinct + column/observations

bn_quantile_bins ADDITIONALLY: probs + quantile_type (ALWAYS 7 — so that two fits are comparable ONLY if they come from the SAME estimator) + n_bins_requested + n_breaks_dropped + dedupe_breaks + data_min/data_max
bn_equal_width ADDITIONALLY: width + range_min/range_max + range_supplied (WHETHER the boundaries are EXOGENOUS or sample-based) + data_min/data_max
interpretation_traps: §3b GATE 6 (fit/apply externalization) — WHY THERE ARE THREE FUNCTIONS: the fit LEARNS the breaks from the sample; a re-fit on new data gives DIFFERENT boundaries => the regime dummies are NOT comparable and the out-of-sample result is «reproducible ONLY BY LUCK». That is why the breaks are returned AS A NUMERIC FIELD and bn_apply accepts them BACK (the KNIME «Auto-Binner» -> PMML model / Normalizer -> «Normalize Model» pattern)

§3b GATE 3 (NON-STATIONARITY, Hamilton-Ma-Xi NBER WP 32068): on an I(1) series the SAMPLE quantiles do NOT converge to a population parameter => the «quartiles» reflect the POSITION IN TIME (the early period = a low bin) and NOT an economic regime. A documented PRECONDITION: discretise DIFFERENCES/rates, or use bn_equal_width with THEORETICAL exogenous boundaries. NEVER a silent correction here (§3b gate 2: no hidden conversion)

DETERMINISM #1 (§5): THE QUANTILE TYPE IS PINNED TO 7 (the conventional default) and is NOT exposed as an argument: the NINE types of Hyndman & Fan (1996) give DIFFERENT breaks on the SAME data, so a switchable 'type' would break the reproducibility of STORED workflows («stored workflows pin node versions», §5). The type is ALWAYS returned in quantile_type

DETERMINISM #2: the equal-width boundaries are computed EXPLICITLY as n_bins+1 evenly spaced edges — NEVER by asking the cut routine for a bin COUNT, which SILENTLY MOVES the outer limits by 0.1% of the range (documented) AND does not report the boundaries it used, giving a fit that cannot be externalized and breaking gate 6. There is no randomness, sampling or parallelism; two identical runs are pinned in the tests, for both the wrapper and the node

SILENTLY WRONG (a): VALUES OUTSIDE the breaks come back SILENTLY blank — the documentation states that they are coded as missing; in an out-of-sample apply that means LOST OBSERVATIONS WITH NO INDICATION ⇒ an explicit out_of_range policy, defaulting to 'fail'

SILENTLY WRONG (cut b): UNSORTED breaks are sorted SILENTLY («The default method will sort a numeric vector of breaks») AND the labels are matched AFTER the sorting => the REGIME NAMES land on the WRONG BINS. A hard gate: STRICTLY INCREASING breaks

SILENTLY WRONG (c to f): a blank INSIDE the breaks is ignored SILENTLY, giving ONE bin instead of two; DUPLICATE labels are MERGED SILENTLY into ONE level, so every value lands in it; breaks given as a categorical use the LEVEL CODES SILENTLY; include_lowest=False blanks the MINIMUM value SILENTLY; and an infinity in the data gives a blank bin SILENTLY. ALL are hard gates

SILENTLY WRONG (number of bins): n_bins = 1 is not a discretisation — cut with 2 breaks returns ONE level WITHOUT an error => a gate n_bins >= 2 AND STRICTLY < the number of UNIQUE values (otherwise the boundaries coincide)

TIES (the most frequent real cause of failure): on a column with many repetitions the quantiles COINCIDE and the cut routine throws «'breaks' are not unique». The node catches it BEFORE the call, naming the column and counting the duplicates; the ways out are to lower n_bins, or to consent explicitly with dedupe_breaks=True, which then gives FEWER bins, no longer of equal population. In bn_apply duplicates are ALWAYS A HARD STOP — deduping there would change the number of bins relative to the fit

MISSING-VALUE POLICY: na_action='fail' (the default) or 'keep' — NEVER 'omit'. The regime dummies MUST stay ALIGNED with the series or the panel, and removing rows would break the alignment with y — exactly the mistake the model frame makes silently, see #253. With 'keep' the missing POSITIONS are preserved with a blank code and recorded in n_missing and missing_index

right and include_lowest MUST be THE SAME in the apply as in the fit — the fits here are ALWAYS include_lowest=True — otherwise the BOUNDARY observations change bin; and out_of_range='clamp' REQUIRES include_lowest=True, since a value clamped onto the extreme boundary would otherwise come back blank AGAIN

THE OUTPUT IS NEVER a categorical object: it is kept INTERNALLY and DECOMPOSED into INTEGER codes plus text labels (JSON-safe, §5); the ORDERING lives in the order of 'labels', which is why the ordered-result switch is omitted; the label precision is PINNED to 3 significant digits, the reference default, with a post-check on uniqueness and the level count — the routine itself raises the precision as far as 12 digits, and falls back to 'Range_k' labels when the boundaries differ only at the fourteenth digit (live-verified)

A TERMINAL node (no register/chaining): it returns chart-ready numbers (codes/labels per observation, breaks, per-bin counts/share/boundaries/observed min-max-mean-median, an optional 0/1 matrix). The fit/apply is EXPLICIT: the user hands the breaks back

cards.method: Series splicing, linking and backcasting
cards.when: two or more overlapping vintages of the same concept must become one continuous series -- rebased indices, reclassified aggregates, a discontinued series continued by a successor
cards.when_not: the series share no overlap and no ratio can be computed; the break is a genuine level change that should be modelled, not spliced away

alternatives.criterion: an overlap period exists
the series are in levels and an additive link is right
no overlap, but a related indicator spans the gap

output_key_fields: spliced: the continuous series
link_factor: the ratio or difference applied, per join
overlap_periods: how many periods the link rested on
breaks: the join dates, retained so the splice is auditable
interpretation_traps: a splice computed on ONE overlapping observation is a rescaling of noise; report the overlap length beside the factor
ratio splicing preserves growth rates and distorts levels; difference splicing does the reverse -- the choice is substantive
a spliced series carries a discontinuity in its second moment even when the level is smooth, which shows up later as a spurious volatility break
sources: Eurostat 2018, Handbook on Rapid Estimates, ch.6
IMF 2018, Quarterly National Accounts Manual

cards.method: Chain linking with an explicit non-additivity residual
cards.when: converting fixed-base volume measures into chain-linked ones, and showing the non-additivity that chain linking necessarily creates
cards.when_not: the data are already chain linked; the components have no consistent price and volume split

alternatives.criterion: the standard national-accounts convention
quarterly data and you follow that convention
the series is strongly seasonal

output_key_fields: chained: the chain-linked volume series
residual: the non-additivity, components minus aggregate
reference_year: the year levels are expressed in
contributions: additive growth contributions, which remain valid
interpretation_traps: CHAIN-LINKED VOLUMES DO NOT ADD UP; the residual is a property of the method, not an error, and suppressing it hides a real feature of the data
the linking convention -- annual overlap, one-quarter overlap, over-the-year -- changes the result and must be stated
growth contributions remain additive even when levels do not; report contributions rather than level shares
sources: Eurostat 2013, Handbook on Quarterly National Accounts, ch.6
IMF 2018, Quarterly National Accounts Manual, ch.8

cards.method: Currency, purchasing-power-parity and constant-price conversion with group aggregates
cards.when: putting series from different countries or periods onto one comparable basis, and aggregating them into a group total
cards.when_not: the conversion factors are unavailable for the periods needed; the concept is not comparable regardless of the units

alternatives.criterion: the question is financial or trade flows
the question is real income or welfare comparison
the question is volume change over time

output_key_fields: converted: the series on the common basis
aggregate: the group total or weighted mean
weights: the weights used for the aggregate
basis: the conversion applied, echoed for auditability
interpretation_traps: MARKET RATES AND PPPs GIVE VERY DIFFERENT ANSWERS -- often by a factor of two or more for emerging economies -- and which is right depends entirely on the question
converting then aggregating and aggregating then converting are not the same when weights differ; state the order
a constant-price series is only comparable within one base period; re-basing changes growth rates through weighting
sources: OECD 2012, Eurostat-OECD Methodological Manual on Purchasing Power Parities
World Bank International Comparison Program documentation

cards.method: Trading-day, leap-year and Easter regressors
cards.when: building the calendar variables a seasonal-adjustment or forecasting model needs, so composition-of-the-month effects do not masquerade as seasonality
cards.when_not: the data are annual, where calendar effects do not arise; the series is not flow data and has no trading-day sensitivity

alternatives.criterion: the number of each weekday in the period matters
only the working/non-working split matters
a holiday moves between periods

output_key_fields: regressors: the constructed calendar matrix
trading_day: weekday-count contrasts, summing to zero by construction
leap_year: the February length correction
easter: the moving-holiday proximity variable
interpretation_traps: trading-day regressors are CONTRASTS and must sum to zero, or they are collinear with the mean and the model will not identify them
the Easter regressor depends on an assumed window length before the holiday; the choice changes the estimated effect
applying trading-day adjustment to a stock series rather than a flow series introduces an effect that was not there
sources: Findley, Monsell, Bell, Otto & Chen 1998 (Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 16:127-152)
U.S. Census Bureau X-13ARIMA-SEATS Reference Manual
statsmodels

cards.method: Multivariate imputation: MICE, iterative, KNN and EM
cards.when: missing values are scattered across several variables and dropping incomplete rows would discard most of the sample or bias it
cards.when_not: the data are missing not at random, where every method here is biased and the missingness must be modelled; a single variable is missing and a simpler method suffices

alternatives.criterion: you want valid inference reflecting imputation uncertainty
you only need a completed dataset for a downstream fit
the structure is local and nonlinear

output_key_fields: imputed: the completed dataset, or the stack of imputations
n_imputations: how many were produced
convergence: chain diagnostics for the iterative methods
missingness_pattern: the pattern the imputation was fitted against
interpretation_traps: SINGLE imputation understates uncertainty because it treats imputed values as observed; multiple imputation with Rubin's rules is what fixes it
the imputation model must include the analysis model's variables -- including the outcome -- or the imputation biases the relationships you go on to estimate
all of these assume missing at random; nothing in the data can verify that assumption
sources: Rubin 1987, Multiple Imputation for Nonresponse in Surveys
van Buuren & Groothuis-Oudshoorn 2011 (Journal of Statistical Software 45:1-67)
miceforest

cards.method: Deterministic-term generator: seasonal dummies, Fourier harmonics and trends
cards.when: building the deterministic regressors a time-series model needs, consistently between the estimation sample and the forecast horizon
cards.when_not: the model generates its own deterministic terms internally; the series has no deterministic component

alternatives.criterion: few seasons and you want an unrestricted pattern
many seasons or multiple seasonalities, and you want few parameters
a smooth deterministic trend is wanted

output_key_fields: terms: the constructed regressor matrix
out_of_sample: the same terms extended over the forecast horizon
names: column names, so coefficients remain interpretable
rank: the matrix rank, which reveals collinearity with an intercept
interpretation_traps: seasonal dummies plus an intercept are COLLINEAR unless one season is dropped or the dummies are centred; the generator must state which convention it used
the out-of-sample terms must be generated by the SAME rule as the in-sample ones -- regenerating them independently is a classic source of forecast breaks
too many Fourier harmonics reproduce the dummies exactly and lose the parsimony that motivated them
sources: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos 2021, Forecasting: Principles and Practice, 3rd ed., ch.7
statsmodels.tsa.deterministic

cards.method: Kernel density and empirical distribution grids
cards.when: producing the density or distribution-function values other methods consume -- risk measures, quantile mappings, distributional plots
cards.when_not: you need the density estimated conditionally (-> conditional KDE); the tail beyond the data matters (-> extreme value theory)

alternatives.criterion: a smooth density is wanted
no smoothing, exact at the observations
a coarse, fast summary

output_key_fields: density: the estimated density on the grid
cdf: the distribution function on the same grid
grid: the evaluation points
bandwidth: the smoothing applied
interpretation_traps: kernel density estimates are BIASED AT A HARD BOUNDARY such as zero; reflect or transform first for durations, shares and non-negative variables
the empirical CDF is a step function, so quantiles read off it are not unique between observations
grid resolution silently determines how much structure is visible; a coarse grid hides multimodality
sources: Silverman 1986, Density Estimation for Statistics and Data Analysis
Sheather & Jones 1991 (JRSS-B 53:683-690)
KDEpy

cards.method: Schema validation and data contracts
cards.when: refusing bad data at the door instead of discovering it in a result -- types, ranges, uniqueness and nullability asserted before anything is computed
cards.when_not: the data are already validated upstream; the schema cannot be stated because the shape is genuinely unknown

alternatives.criterion: the shape is known and should be enforced
the shape is unknown and you want to discover it first
one or two checks only

output_key_fields: valid: whether the table satisfied the contract
failures: which rows and columns failed which check
coerced: values changed by type coercion, where it was permitted
schema: the contract that was applied
interpretation_traps: a validator run in permissive mode COERCES rather than refuses, which turns a loud failure into a silent change of data
checks that examine zero rows pass trivially; an empty table must fail validation, not sail through it
validating after the analysis has already run tells you the result was wrong, which is later than it needed to be
sources: Pandera documentation
Polyzotis, Roy, Whang & Zinkevich 2018 (SIGMOD Record 47:17-28)

cards.method: Record linkage, deduplication and fuzzy matching
cards.when: joining two datasets that share no key, or removing duplicate entities from one, using approximate agreement across several fields
cards.when_not: a reliable shared key exists (join on it); the datasets are so large that blocking is infeasible without a specialised backend

alternatives.criterion: a key exists and only formatting differs
no key, and agreement patterns must be weighted
the task is within one dataset

output_key_fields: matches: the accepted linked pairs with their scores
candidate_pairs: how many comparisons blocking produced
threshold: the score cut-off applied
reduction_ratio: how much blocking reduced the comparison space
interpretation_traps: BLOCKING determines what can ever be matched: a pair excluded by the blocking key can never be linked, however similar it is
the threshold trades false links against missed ones and there is no neutral choice; report the score distribution, not just the count
transitivity fails -- A matches B and B matches C does not make A and C the same entity, and naive clustering will merge them
sources: Fellegi & Sunter 1969 (JASA 64:1183-1210)
Christen 2012, Data Matching
recordlinkage

cards.method: Formula parsing and the design-matrix contract
cards.when: turning a model formula into the design matrix an estimator consumes, with the same treatment of factors, interactions and missing values every time
cards.when_not: the design matrix is already built; the formula language cannot express the term you need

alternatives.criterion: the standard route from specification to matrix
the design is not expressible as a formula
you want splines or polynomials inside the formula

output_key_fields: design: the constructed design matrix
terms: term names and the columns each produced
contrasts: the coding applied to each factor
dropped: rows dropped for missing values
interpretation_traps: FACTOR CODING is a substantive choice -- treatment, sum and Helmert contrasts give different coefficients from the same data and only the fitted values agree
the design matrix drops rows with missing values silently unless told otherwise, so the estimation sample can differ from the input without warning
the same formula applied to new data can produce different columns if a factor level is absent; the levels must be carried, not re-inferred
sources: Wilkinson & Rogers 1973 (Applied Statistics 22:392-399)
formulaic documentation

cards.method: Compositional log-ratio transforms: CLR, ILR and ALR
cards.when: the variables are shares that sum to a constant, so ordinary statistics on them are invalid -- correlations are spuriously negative and variances are not free
cards.when_not: the data are not compositional; there are structural zeros that no log-ratio transform can handle without imputation

alternatives.criterion: you want a symmetric transform keeping all parts
you need a full-rank basis for multivariate methods
one part is a natural reference denominator

output_key_fields: transformed: the data in log-ratio coordinates
basis: the basis used, needed to invert the transform
zeros_handled: how zeros were treated, which is the main practical issue
inverse: the back-transform to the simplex
interpretation_traps: log-ratio transforms are UNDEFINED AT ZERO; zero replacement is a modelling decision that changes results and must be reported, not hidden in a default
the CLR-transformed data are singular by construction -- their covariance matrix is rank deficient, which breaks methods requiring invertibility; ILR exists for that
correlations between raw shares are spuriously negative because the parts sum to a constant; interpreting them is the error this whole card exists to prevent
sources: Aitchison 1986, The Statistical Analysis of Compositional Data
Egozcue, Pawlowsky-Glahn, Mateu-Figueras & Barcelo-Vidal 2003 (Mathematical Geology 35:279-300)
composition-stats

cards.method: Columnar and lazy execution for large panels
cards.when: the panel is larger than comfortable in memory, and the operations are filters, joins and group-bys that a columnar engine can stream
cards.when_not: the data fit comfortably in memory and the added indirection is not worth it; the operation is inherently row-wise and iterative

alternatives.criterion: the data are small
the data are large and the pipeline is relational
the operation cannot be expressed relationally

output_key_fields: result: the materialised output
plan: the query plan, before and after optimisation
rows_scanned: how much data the plan actually read
peak_memory: the high-water mark of the execution
interpretation_traps: a LAZY plan does nothing until collected; timing the plan construction rather than the collection measures nothing
predicate pushdown only works if the filter is expressible in the plan -- a filter applied after collection reads the whole dataset first
type coercion rules differ from row-wise engines, and silent upcasting of integers to floats changes joins on keys
sources: Abadi, Boncz & Harizopoulos 2009, Column-oriented database systems (VLDB Endowment 2:1664)

arguments.name: x
arguments.description: Handle to ONE numeric column (n×1: rows = observations/periods/countries). One node PER variable — for several columns do a fan-out. NO NA/NaN/Inf unless na_action='keep' is declared. CAUTION (non-stationarity): in I(1) LEVELS the sample quantiles reflect the POSITION IN TIME and not an economic regime — give DIFFERENCES/rates, or use bn_equal_width with exogenous boundaries (Hamilton-Ma-Xi).

arguments.name: breaks
arguments.description: FIT/APPLY EXTERNALIZATION (§3b gate 6): EXACTLY the 'breaks' field of a PREVIOUS bn_quantile_bins/bn_equal_width. STRICTLY INCREASING, finite, >= 3 points. WITHOUT it, a re-fit on the new data gives DIFFERENT boundaries and the regime dummies are NOT comparable with the training sample. DUPLICATE/unsorted boundaries are blocked: the binning routine sorts SILENTLY and the labels move to the WRONG bins.

arguments.name: labels
arguments.description: Names of the bins (e.g. ['low','mid','high'] or ['Q1','Q2','Q3','Q4']) — EXACTLY n_bins in count, UNIQUE and non-empty. Omitting them produces the intervals of the binning routine ('(a,b]'). DUPLICATE labels ARE BLOCKED: the binning routine MERGES them SILENTLY into ONE level, so two bins become one (silent-wrong).

arguments.name: right
arguments.description: True (default, like the binning routine) = intervals CLOSED ON THE RIGHT: (b1,b2]... (bk-1,bk]. False = [b1,b2)... [bk-1,bk). The EXTREME point is always included (include.lowest = True in the fit). IN bn_apply it MUST be THE SAME as in the fit, otherwise the boundary observations change bin.

arguments.name: include_lowest
arguments.description: True (default) = the EXTREME boundary (the lower one with right=True, the upper one with right=False) belongs to the extreme bin. False = the value that EQUALS the endpoint belongs NOWHERE (the binning routine SILENTLY zeroes it to NA). It MUST be THE SAME as in the fit (the fits here are always True).

arguments.name: out_of_range
arguments.description: Policy for NEW values OUTSIDE the range of the breaks — the binning routine encodes them SILENTLY as NA ("Values which fall outside the range of breaks are coded as NA»), i.e. LOST observations without any indication. 'fail' (default) = blocked-by-gate. 'na' = An EXPLICIT NA code + a record in n_out_of_range/out_of_range_labels. 'clamp' = assignment to the EXTREME bin (requires include_lowest=True); useful when the regimes are defined as "below/above X" but it DISTORTS the extremeness information.

arguments.name: na_action
arguments.description: Policy for NA/NaN/Inf. 'fail' (default) = blocked-by-gate (the quantile estimator throws "missing values and NaN's not allowed if 'the NA policy' is False" and the binning routine encodes Inf SILENTLY as NA). 'keep' = the boundaries are estimated from the FINITE values and the missing positions ARE KEPT with an NA code — rows are NEVER removed, so that the regime dummies stay ALIGNED with y.

arguments.name: dummies
arguments.description: True = it also returns the 0/1 indicator matrix (n×n_bins, ONE column per bin) — ready REGIME DUMMIES for regression. The missing/out-of-range rows get NA (NOT 0: 0 would mean "definitely not in this bin"). Default False (smaller payload).

arguments.name: cutoff

STRICTLY inside (0,1): the upstream routine does NOT check — with cutoff = 1.5 it silently filters NOTHING and with cutoff <= 0 it removes almost EVERYTHING.
